why: The BOOT half of the future-schema contract, one layer above `settings-future-payload-overwritten`: that entry mutates a later write, this one makes the PARSER classify a version-2 payload as junk. Under it the store reports `schema: 'recovered'` rather than `'future'`, stops reporting `storedVersion`, drops the `locked-future` persistence state -- so the notice becomes the wrong one -- and becomes eligible for legacy migration, which would adopt older values over a newer build's payload. Killed by settings.test.ts's future-payload status assertions and the 'never migrates the legacy key over a future payload' case, plus app-settings.test.ts's future-schema notice. 4 of 55 across the two declared files.
